# Depth audit — 2026-09-28

<!-- depth-audit:begin — generated by tools/depth-audit.js; do not edit by hand -->

## What this is, and what it is not

A **generated** pass over every lab-shaped repository in the organisation, derived from
an export of each remote default branch. It extends rather than replaces the hand-read
[2026-09-25 audit](DEPTH-AUDIT-2026-09-25.md) and [its follow-up](DEPTH-AUDIT-FOLLOWUP-2026-09-26.md),
which stated their own limit plainly: source-scan coverage is not dimension coverage, most
labs carried `?` on the dimensions that weigh most, and neither would rank from partial
scores. This file exists to make those dimensions derivable, and re-derivable — the reports
above are snapshots of a fleet that moves, and `node tools/depth-audit.js check` fails when
this one drifts from the exports it was built from.

It is a record of **what is tested and by what**. It is not a security assessment, and no
row here should be read as saying a lab is secure, correct, or verified.

**A lexical hit is a lead, not proof.** That rule is inherited from the 2026-09-25 audit and
governs ground truth: a file naming a standard with no fixed material beside it is recorded
as unresolved, not as credited.

## Coverage

| Scope | Labs | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Remote default branches exported and read | 211 | Every lab-shaped repository the organisation lists |
| Export failures | 0 | A repository that could not be read would appear here, not as a low score |
| Carrying source in a language this tool does not read | 15 | Reported per lab; those dimensions stay unresolved rather than scoring zero |
| Carrying vendored paths, omitted from the read | 3 | First-party findings are a floor for these |
| In a course module | 5 | Derived from `teach/_src`; first ranking key |

| Dimension | Weight | Credited when | Unresolved |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| T ground truth | 4 | a named published source cited beside fixed material | 27 |
| I independent check | 4 | a test reads an outside implementation, or a separate verification script runs | 0 |
| C displayed claim | 2 | a test compares a RENDERED value with one the code computed, not with a literal | 1 |
| N negative test | 2 | a throw, rejection, or a case named for the failure it forces | 0 |
| G deploy gate | 2 | the publishing workflow runs a test step; engines are named, never inferred | 1 |
| H limits and guidance | 1 | README states scale or limits | 0 |

`+` credited · `0` inspected and not met · `?` not derivable here. **A `?` is excluded from
both the earned and the assessed weight**, so an unknown is never averaged into a score.
Two scores with different assessed weights are not comparable as fractions.

**The displayed-claim dimension was rebuilt after it failed to discriminate.** It first
credited the PRESENCE of a claims spec, and measurement showed what that was worth: every
lab with such a file scored credited and every lab without it did not. A column everything
passes inflates every rank it appears in. It now requires an assertion whose expected side
is an expression rather than a literal — a page panel reading "0 hex digits differ" is
checked against a sentence someone typed, while one equal to `digestBefore` is checked
against the computation.

**The seventh dimension is not scored here.** Whether a test step runs and reports zero
tests is credited in this rubric only on observed run output, which is file-invisible.
That evidence is gathered against pinned commits in
[the observed-test-runs supplement](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/crypto-lab/pull/29).
What this tool can see is the structural hazard that makes a zero-test run possible, and it
reports that separately below rather than scoring a weaker answer to the same question.

## Calibration against the hand-read audit

The labs the [2026-09-25 audit](DEPTH-AUDIT-2026-09-25.md) named as references, scored again
by this tool. Disagreement is recorded rather than tuned away: where a careful reader and a
derivation differ, the difference is usually definitional and worth seeing.

| Lab | This tool | Reference by this rule | Where the two differ |
|---|---:|---|---|
| kem-trap | 13/15 | no | this tool records C as inspected and not met, where the hand read left them unresolved |
| drbg-arena | 11/15 | no | this tool records I as inspected and not met, where the hand read left them unresolved |
| webauthn | 5/15 | no | this tool records T, I, C as inspected and not met, where the hand read left them unresolved |
| frost-threshold | 13/15 | no | this tool records C as inspected and not met, where the hand read left them unresolved |
| protocol-checker | 7/15 | no | this tool records T, I as inspected and not met, where the hand read left them unresolved |
| ec-point-arithmetic | 11/15 | no | this tool records T as inspected and not met, where the hand read left them unresolved |
| attribute-gate | 15/15 | yes | agrees |

A dimension this tool marks `0` and a hand reader marked `?` is the commonest difference,
and it is a real one: `0` says the files were read and the thing is not there, `?` says the
question was not settled. The stricter mark is only better where the derivation is sound, so
the ledger below carries the anchor for every credited dimension and nothing else is claimed.
